extracted.intended_audience: authors, peer reviewers, journal editors, and funders involved in reporting animal (in vivo) research
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for preparing and assessing scientific manuscripts that report experiments using animals (in vivo), specifying the minimum information to ensure completeness, transparency, reproducibility, and humane practice. Intended to be used by authors when writing manuscripts and by peer reviewers, editors, and funders for quality assurance.

rubrics_metrics.name: TITLE
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide as accurate and concise a description of the content of the article as possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: ABSTRACT
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide an accurate summary of the background, research objectives (including details of the species or strain of animal used), key methods, principal findings, and conclusions of the study.

rubrics_metrics.name: INTRODUCTION: Background
rubrics_metrics.description: Include sufficient scientific background (including relevant references to previous work) to understand the motivation and context for the study, and explain the experimental approach and rationale.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where appropriate, include the study’s relevance to human biology.

rubrics_metrics.name: INTRODUCTION: Objectives
rubrics_metrics.description: Clearly describe the primary and any secondary objectives of the study, or specific hypotheses being tested.

rubrics_metrics.name: METHODS: Ethical statement
rubrics_metrics.description: Indicate the nature of the ethical review permissions, relevant licences (e.g. Animal [Scientific Procedures] Act 1986), and national or institutional guidelines for the care and use of animals, that cover the research.

rubrics_metrics.name: METHODS: Study design
rubrics_metrics.description: The number of experimental and control groups; for each experiment, give brief details of the study design.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For each experiment describe: a) the experimental unit (e.g. a single animal, group, or cage of animals); b) any steps taken to minimise the effects of subjective bias when allocating animals to treatment (e.g., randomisation procedure) and when assessing results (e.g., who was blinded and when); c) a time-line diagram or flow chart can be useful to illustrate how complex study designs were carried out.

rubrics_metrics.name: METHODS: Experimental procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: For each experiment and each experimental group, including controls, provide precise details of all procedures carried out.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include details such as: a) How (e.g., drug formulation and dose, site and route of administration, anaesthesia and analgesia used [including monitoring], surgical procedure, method of euthanasia). Provide details of any specialist equipment used, including supplier(s). b) When (e.g., time of day). c) Where (e.g., home cage, laboratory, water maze). d) Why (e.g., rationale for choice of specific anaesthetic, route of administration, drug dose used).

rubrics_metrics.name: METHODS: Experimental animals
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide details of the animals used, including species, strain, sex, developmental stage (e.g., mean or median age plus age range), and weight (e.g., mean or median weight plus weight range).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Also provide further relevant information such as the source of animals, international strain nomenclature, genetic modification status (e.g. knock-out or transgenic), genotype, health/immune status, drug- or test-naı̈ve, previous procedures, etc.

rubrics_metrics.name: METHODS: Housing and husbandry
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide details of housing and husbandry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include: a) Housing (e.g., type of facility, e.g., specific pathogen free (SPF); type of cage or housing; bedding material; number of cage companions; tank shape and material etc. for fish). b) Husbandry conditions (e.g., breeding programme, light/dark cycle, temperature, quality of water etc. for fish, type of food, access to food and water, environmental enrichment). c) Welfare-related assessments and interventions that were carried out before, during, or after the experiment.

rubrics_metrics.name: METHODS: Sample size
rubrics_metrics.description: Specify the total number of animals used in each experiment and the number of animals in each experimental group.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain how the number of animals was decided. Provide details of any sample size calculation used. Indicate the number of independent replications of each experiment, if relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: METHODS: Allocating animals to experimental groups
rubrics_metrics.description: Give full details of how animals were allocated to experimental groups, including randomisation or matching if done.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe the order in which the animals in the different experimental groups were treated and assessed.

rubrics_metrics.name: METHODS: Experimental outcomes
rubrics_metrics.description: Clearly define the primary and secondary experimental outcomes assessed (e.g., cell death, molecular markers, behavioural changes).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specify the unit of analysis for each dataset (e.g. single animal, group of animals, single neuron).

rubrics_metrics.name: METHODS: Statistical methods
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide details of the statistical methods used for each analysis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe any methods used to assess whether the data met the assumptions of the statistical approach, and specify the unit of analysis for each dataset where relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: RESULTS: Baseline data
rubrics_metrics.description: For each experimental group, report relevant characteristics and health status of animals (e.g., weight, microbiological status, and drug- or test-naı̈ve) before treatment or testing (this information can often be tabulated).

rubrics_metrics.name: RESULTS: Numbers analysed
rubrics_metrics.description: Report the number of animals in each group included in each analysis. Report absolute numbers (e.g. 10/20, not 50%).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If any animals or data were not included in the analysis, explain why.

rubrics_metrics.name: RESULTS: Outcomes and estimation
rubrics_metrics.description: Report the results for each analysis carried out, with a measure of precision (e.g., standard error or confidence interval).

rubrics_metrics.name: RESULTS: Adverse events
rubrics_metrics.description: Give details of all important adverse events in each experimental group.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe any modifications to the experimental protocols made to reduce adverse events.

rubrics_metrics.name: DISCUSSION: Interpretation/scientific implications (Item 18)
rubrics_metrics.description: Interpret the results, taking into account the study objectives and hypotheses, current theory, and other relevant studies in the literature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: a) Comment on the study limitations including any potential sources of bias, any limitations of the animal model, and the imprecision associated with the results. b) Describe any implications of your experimental methods or findings for the replacement, refinement, or reduction (the 3Rs) of the use of animals in research.

rubrics_metrics.name: DISCUSSION: Generalisability/translation (Item 19)
rubrics_metrics.description: Comment on whether, and how, the findings of this study are likely to translate to other species or systems, including any relevance to human biology.

rubrics_metrics.name: DISCUSSION: Funding (Item 20)
rubrics_metrics.description: List all funding sources (including grant number) and the role of the funder(s) in the study.
